`test_get_inventory` and `test_get_products` both failed in [Daily CI run 537](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/32853814132>) with "no inventory returned" / "no products returned", and reproduce locally.

The inventory call answers 200 with an empty payload:

```json
{"client": "UW", "inventory": null, "other": null}
```

A bad client code comes back as a 400 "Invalid Client" instead (established in #5693), so client UW is valid and simply holds no stock. Capacity passed in run 536 the day before, so the sandbox emptied between the two runs.

Nothing to fix in our code. We also cannot put the stock back: `allow_writes()` is `False` on this connection and `test_account()` describes it as a read-only Flexport sandbox.

Next step is a human deciding between asking Flexport to restock the sandbox client, pointing the test at a client that has stock, or accepting an empty inventory the way `test_get_orders` and `test_get_inbound_shipments` already do on this integration (both skip with a written reason).

Triaged in [trackstarhq/pokedex#5724](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/review/fix-tests-daily-ci-run-537-cart-walmart-clarus-aba4d75a2b7f).

```
Test: test/integrations/wms/capacity_test.py::TestCapacity::test_get_inventory
Test: test/integrations/wms/capacity_test.py::TestCapacity::test_get_products
```
>>>>
<<<<TRA-2683
`test_get_orders_auth_code` failed in [Daily CI run 535](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/32489422935>) with `Failed: Timeout (>240.0s) from pytest-timeout`, and reproduces locally in a serial single-worker run (`1 failed, 32 passed, 15 skipped, 1 xfailed in 1189s`).

The time goes into one call, before any order is read:

```
integrations/wms/skuvault/integration.py:824: in get_orders
integrations/wms/skuvault/integration.py:808: in get_kits
integrations/wms/skuvault/integration.py:141: in skuvault_request
integrations/wms/skuvault/integration.py:115: in retry_request
E  Failed: Timeout (>240.0s) from pytest-timeout
```

`get_orders` calls `get_kits()` on the first loop, and `get_kits` posts `products/getKits` with an empty body. That endpoint does not paginate, so it returns the account's entire kit catalog in one response. The code comment on the sibling call in `get_products` says as much: "getKits endpoint doesn't paginate, just returns all kits". On this connection that single request does not come back inside the test's 240s budget.

Same shape as [TRA-2383](<https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2383/fulfilmentcrowd-get-shipping-methods-makes-84-serial-carrier-requests>) on fulfilmentcrowd: one expensive unbounded call sitting right at the timeout, so it flips between runs rather than failing every day. Under the daily suite's 32 workers the latency is worse than measured serially.

Note this is separate from [TRA-2216](<https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2216/skuvault-create-partial-fulfillment-throttled-in-ci-2-days-running>), which is a throttle on `create_partial_fulfillment`.

`test_get_product_auth_code`, which also timed out in run 535, passed locally, so treat that one as transient rather than part of this.

Wants a decision on how to make the kit fetch cheaper. `get_kits` accepts a `KitSKUs` filter, so fetching kits for the SKUs actually on the orders in the window is one option, as is caching the kit map across loops instead of refetching. Deliberately not attempted in the fix-tests sweep: it changes a shared read path used by both `get_orders` and `get_products` and wants its own verification.

From the daily fix-tests triage of [run 535](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/32489422935>).

```
Test: test/integrations/wms/skuvault_test.py::TestSkuvault::test_get_orders_perm_validator
```
>>>>
<<<<TRA-2650
`get_inventory` on the shiphero test connection cannot finish a single page inside the 240s test budget, and ShipHero drops the connection partway through. Red in [Daily CI run 531](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/32145089631>) and reproduced three times locally on 2026-08-18. It was green in run 530, so this is the account crossing a threshold rather than a code change.

**Measured, one page of 50 inventory items** (instrumented `shiphero_request`, 15 day window, `page_token="default"`):

```
1 main warehouse_products query        4.0s
159 get_additional_inv_data queries  135.0s   (slowest single call 11.1s)
wall 139.8s, then:
requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: ('Connection aborted.',
    ConnectionResetError(104, 'Connection reset by peer'))
```

**Why 159.** `get_inventory` asks for only the first 5 inbounds and first 5 locations per warehouse product (`integrations/wms/shiphero/integration.py:404-407`). Anything past that is paged one request at a time in `get_additional_inv_data` (:575-598), serially, per warehouse product. This account now averages about three extra round trips per item, so the follow-up loop is 97% of the wall time.

Two directions, both with rate-limit tradeoffs that want a human call:

* Raise `inbounds_page_size` / `location_page_size` so the first query covers most items. Fewer round trips, but a heavier main query, and ShipHero bills by credit-weighted field, which is what [TRA-2596](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2596/shiphero-get-inventory-page-costs-1301-credits-and-starves-on-the) was trimming.
* Fetch the follow-ups concurrently instead of serially. Same credit cost, much less wall time, but it concentrates the burn and can throttle harder.

Same function and the same serial-scan shape as [TRA-2014](<https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2014/shiphero-get-inventory-backlog-scan-throttles-to-death-cursor-stuck>), which was closed without changing this loop.

`test_get_inventory` stays red until this is picked up.

```
Test: test/integrations/wms/shiphero_test.py::TestShiphero::test_get_inventory
```
>>>>
<<<<TRA-2567
`test_install` fails in the [2026-08-12 daily CI run](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/31607188404>) with:

```
utils.exceptions.PokedexException: FTP connect failed: [Errno 110] Connection timed out
```

The 2026-08-11 sweep recorded this as transient because it passed locally then. It no longer does: reproduced locally today on `main` (f46e719), `1 failed, 47 deselected in 28.95s`, same error. The failure comes back through the FTP proxy lambda (`transports/proxy.py` `proxy_invoke`), so the vendor's FTP host is refusing or dropping connections from the proxy's egress, not a local network problem.

Nothing in pokedex can fix this. Needs someone to confirm with States Logistics that `ftp.stateslogistics.com` is up and that our egress IP is still allowed, then re-check the connection.

Two CI runs in a row (2026-08-11, 2026-08-12) plus a local reproduction.

```
Test: test/integrations/wms/states-logistics_test.py::TestStatesLogistics::test_install
```
>>>>

The time goes into one call, before any order is read:

```
integrations/wms/skuvault/integration.py:824: in get_orders
integrations/wms/skuvault/integration.py:808: in get_kits
integrations/wms/skuvault/integration.py:141: in skuvault_request
integrations/wms/skuvault/integration.py:115: in retry_request
E  Failed: Timeout (>240.0s) from pytest-timeout
```

`get_orders` calls `get_kits()` on the first loop, and `get_kits` posts `products/getKits` with an empty body. That endpoint does not paginate, so it returns the account's entire kit catalog in one response. The code comment on the sibling call in `get_products` says as much: "getKits endpoint doesn't paginate, just returns all kits". On this connection that single request does not come back inside the test's 240s budget.

Same shape as [TRA-2383](<https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2383/fulfilmentcrowd-get-shipping-methods-makes-84-serial-carrier-requests>) on fulfilmentcrowd: one expensive unbounded call sitting right at the timeout, so it flips between runs rather than failing every day. Under the daily suite's 32 workers the latency is worse than measured serially.

Note this is separate from [TRA-2216](<https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2216/skuvault-create-partial-fulfillment-throttled-in-ci-2-days-running>), which is a throttle on `create_partial_fulfillment`.

`test_get_product_auth_code`, which also timed out in run 535, passed locally, so treat that one as transient rather than part of this.

Deliberately not attempted in the fix-tests sweep: it changes a shared read path used by both `get_orders` and `get_products` and wants its own verification.

`get_inventory` on the shiphero test connection cannot finish a single page inside the 240s test budget, and ShipHero drops the connection partway through. Red in [Daily CI run 531](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/32145089631>) and reproduced three times locally on 2026-08-18. It was green in run 530, so this is the account crossing a threshold rather than a code change.

**Measured, one page of 50 inventory items** (instrumented `shiphero_request`, 15 day window, `page_token="default"`):

```
1 main warehouse_products query        4.0s
159 get_additional_inv_data queries  135.0s   (slowest single call 11.1s)
wall 139.8s, then:
requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: ('Connection aborted.',
    ConnectionResetError(104, 'Connection reset by peer'))
```

**Why 159.** `get_inventory` asks for only the first 5 inbounds and first 5 locations per warehouse product (`integrations/wms/shiphero/integration.py:404-407`). Anything past that is paged one request at a time in `get_additional_inv_data` (:575-598), serially, per warehouse product. This account now averages about three extra round trips per item, so the follow-up loop is 97% of the wall time.

Two directions, both with rate-limit tradeoffs that want a human call:

* Raise `inbounds_page_size` / `location_page_size` so the first query covers most items. Fewer round trips, but a heavier main query, and ShipHero bills by credit-weighted field, which is what [TRA-2596](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2596/shiphero-get-inventory-page-costs-1301-credits-and-starves-on-the) was trimming.
* Fetch the follow-ups concurrently instead of serially. Same credit cost, much less wall time, but it concentrates the burn and can throttle harder.

Same function and the same serial-scan shape as [TRA-2014](<https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2014/shiphero-get-inventory-backlog-scan-throttles-to-death-cursor-stuck>), which was closed without changing this loop.

`test_get_inventory` stays red until this is picked up.

```
Test: test/integrations/wms/shiphero_test.py::TestShiphero::test_get_inventory
```

`test_install` fails in the [2026-08-12 daily CI run](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/31607188404>) with:

```
utils.exceptions.PokedexException: FTP connect failed: [Errno 110] Connection timed out
```

The 2026-08-11 sweep recorded this as transient because it passed locally then. It no longer does: reproduced locally today on `main` (f46e719), `1 failed, 47 deselected in 28.95s`, same error. The failure comes back through the FTP proxy lambda (`transports/proxy.py` `proxy_invoke`), so the vendor's FTP host is refusing or dropping connections from the proxy's egress, not a local network problem.

Nothing in pokedex can fix this. Needs someone to confirm with States Logistics that `ftp.stateslogistics.com` is up and that our egress IP is still allowed, then re-check the connection.

Two CI runs in a row (2026-08-11, 2026-08-12) plus a local reproduction.

```
Test: test/integrations/wms/states-logistics_test.py::TestStatesLogistics::test_install
```

It was green in run 530, so this is the account crossing a threshold rather than a code change.

**Measured, one page of 50 inventory items** (instrumented `shiphero_request`, 15 day window, `page_token="default"`):

```
1 main warehouse_products query        4.0s
159 get_additional_inv_data queries  135.0s   (slowest single call 11.1s)
wall 139.8s, then:
requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: ('Connection aborted.',
    ConnectionResetError(104, 'Connection reset by peer'))
```

**Why 159.** `get_inventory` asks for only the first 5 inbounds and first 5 locations per warehouse product (`integrations/wms/shiphero/integration.py:404-407`). Anything past that is paged one request at a time in `get_additional_inv_data` (:575-598), serially, per warehouse product. This account now averages about three extra round trips per item, so the follow-up loop is 97% of the wall time.

Two directions, both with rate-limit tradeoffs that want a human call:

* Raise `inbounds_page_size` / `location_page_size` so the first query covers most items. Fewer round trips, but a heavier main query, and ShipHero bills by credit-weighted field, which is what [TRA-2596](<https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2596/shiphero-get-inventory-page-costs-1301-credits-and-starves-on-the>) was trimming.
* Fetch the follow-ups concurrently instead of serially. Same credit cost, much less wall time, but it concentrates the burn and can throttle harder.

Same function and the same serial-scan shape as [TRA-2014](<https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2014/shiphero-get-inventory-backlog-scan-throttles-to-death-cursor-stuck>), which was closed without changing this loop.

`test_get_inventory` stays red until this is picked up.

utils.exceptions.PokedexException: FTP connect failed: [Errno 110] Connection timed out
```

The 2026-08-11 sweep recorded this as transient because it passed locally then. It no longer does: reproduced locally today on `main` (f46e719), `1 failed, 47 deselected in 28.95s`, same error. Nothing in pokedex can fix this. Needs someone to confirm with States Logistics that `ftp.stateslogistics.com` is up and that our egress IP is still allowed, then re-check the connection.

Two CI runs in a row (2026-08-11, 2026-08-12) plus a local reproduction.

<<<<TRA-2419
New in Daily CI run 518 (2026-07-30). Three `test/api/api_test.py` failures that are one defect plus two cascades.

**Primary.** `test_sandbox_simulate_fulfill` writes a bare `cancelled_order` row (api_test.py:2618) and expects the endpoint to answer 400 "is cancelled". It got 404. The 404 comes from `api.py:2596`, a bare `except` wrapped around `Order(integration).get_resource(order_id)`, so any exception in the lookup reads as "not found in sandbox".

```
FAILED test/api/api_test.py::test_sandbox_simulate_fulfill - assert 404 == 400
```

**Cascade.** The failed assertion skips the `delete_resource` cleanup on the following line, so an order row with no `reference_id` is left in the table. `make_sure_sandbox_orders_testable` (api_test.py:3188) then reads `order["reference_id"]` on every order with no guard:

```
FAILED test/api/api_test.py::test_filters - KeyError: 'reference_id'
FAILED test/api/api_test.py::test_indexes - KeyError: 'reference_id'
```

`--dist=loadfile` runs all three in one worker in file order, and simulate-fulfill is first, so the ordering holds. Worth making the helper tolerate a row without `reference_id` regardless, so one broken test cannot take two others with it.

**Not diagnosed further.** The fix-tests routine could not reproduce this. The api fixtures create a secret and the routine container runs as `read-only-bot-user`:

```
botocore.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the
CreateSecret operation: User: arn:aws:iam::708459675662:user/read-only-bot-user is not
authorized to perform: secretsmanager:CreateSecret
```

Two commits touched `utils/api.py` after run 517 was green and are the candidates for the 404: [trackstarhq/pokedex#5262](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/review/add-completed-at-and-cancelled-at-timestamps-to-sync-jobs-e16082438baa) (sync-job timestamps) and [#5047](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/pull/5047>) (`@function` tag on api writes). Neither is confirmed.

Triage: [Daily CI run 518](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/30556305238>) · [trackstarhq/pokedex#5270](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/review/fix-tests-2026-07-30-skuvault-records-the-success-side-of-api-call-377f7a66af86)

```
Test: test/api/api_test.py::test_sandbox_simulate_fulfill
Test: test/api/api_test.py::test_filters
Test: test/api/api_test.py::test_indexes
```
>>>>
<<<<TRA-2383
`test_get_shipping_methods_auth_code` failed in [Daily CI run 515](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/30281811342>) with `Failed: Timeout (>240.0s) from pytest-timeout`, and reproduces locally in the full auth run (1 failed / 6 passed / 3 skipped, 452s).

`get_shipping_methods` fetches the carrier list, then issues one `carriers/{id}/carrier_services` request per carrier, serially. Measured against the test connection:

```
carriers=84 fetch=1.0s
  carrier 929: 1.2s
  carrier 963: 1.0s
  carrier 1068: 0.9s
  carrier 1069: 0.9s
  carrier 1499: 1.0s
avg per carrier=1.0s -> projected total=87s
```

So the walk costs somewhere north of 87 seconds of pure round-trip time before any latency variance. That is comfortably inside 240s on a good run (the non-auth `test_get_shipping_methods` passed in the same session) and over it on a bad one, which is why this flips between runs rather than failing consistently. Under the daily suite's `-n 32` parallelism the per-request latency is worse than measured here.

Not a defect in the auth-code path: `fc_request` is identical with and without an auth code, and `get_shipping_methods` never touches stored resources. The unrelated auth-code bug in `get_orders` was fixed in [trackstarhq/pokedex#5196](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/review/fix-tests-2026-07-27-excelsior-product-path-and-fulfilmentcrowd-auth-00b69127056c); this one is untouched by that change.

Wants a decision on how to make the walk cheaper, since no bulk carrier-services endpoint is in use today. Deliberately not attempted in the fix-tests sweep: it is a performance change to a shipping path, not a test fix, and it wants its own verification.

```
Test: test/integrations/wms/fulfilmentcrowd_test.py::TestFulfilmentCrowd::test_get_shipping_methods_perm_validator
```
>>>>
<<<<TRA-2369
`test_create_return` fails against a healthy sandbox host with the vendor rejecting the return:

```
PokedexException: {"error":{"message":"Order not found.","specifics":{"data":{
  "http_status":400,"code":"V5-ORDER-INVALID-ORDER","message":"Order not found."}}}}
```

Cause looks like the test fixture, not the integration. `TestIFulfilment.full_return` sets `reference_id` to a fresh `uuid.uuid4().hex`, and `create_return` posts that straight through as the `reference` on `POST /v1/orders/returns`. A random reference matches no order, so the vendor is right to reject it. A return needs the reference of an order that actually exists, presumably the one `test_create_order` just created (which is available via `context`, and note `create_order` reads the reference back off the response as `full_order_ref`, so the vendor may not echo the reference it was given).

This has been failing for a while but was masked. While the sandbox host was hanging it surfaced as `Failed: Timeout (>60.0s) from pytest-timeout`, so it read as part of the outage. With the host healthy the whole suite now runs in 56s and this is the only remaining failure: 1 failed, 21 passed, 26 skipped.

Found on [run 30229827096](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/30229827096>) while confirming [PR #5186](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/pull/5186>), which is unrelated (it only touches the warehouse map in `get_orders`). Not fixed there to keep that PR scoped, and because the fix touches a write test that fires real vendor writes.

Separate from [TRA-2309](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2309/i-fulfilment-test-create-order-indexerror-on-degraded-sandbox-host) (create_order IndexError) and [TRA-1995](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-1995/i-fulfilment-create-order-broken-post-v1orders-returns-404-unknown) (create_order 404).

```
Test: test/integrations/wms/i-fulfilment_test.py::TestIFulfilment::test_create_return
```
>>>>
<<<<TRA-2309
i-fulfilment test_create_order failed in run #511 (2026-07-21) with IndexError: list index out of range at [integration.py:839](<http://integration.py:839>). create_order POSTs the order, then queries orders/goodsouts by the order reference and reads rsp["data"][0]; the goodsouts query came back empty, so the index blew up.

This is almost certainly the same degraded i-fulfilment sandbox host from [TRA-2277](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2277/i-fulfilment-vendor-sandbox-host-hangs-on-data-endpoints-crawls-time) ([public-api-sandbox.staging.bladepro.co.uk](<http://public-api-sandbox.staging.bladepro.co.uk>) accepts TLS but stalls/empties on data endpoints). Different i-fulfilment test has failed each of the last two daily runs (yesterday: get_inbound_shipments "none returned"), which fits an unstable sandbox rather than a single code path. Write test, not re-run here.

Action: primarily a vendor-sandbox issue (see [TRA-2277](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/issue/TRA-2277/i-fulfilment-vendor-sandbox-host-hangs-on-data-endpoints-crawls-time)). A defensive improvement worth considering once the sandbox is healthy: raise a clear PokedexException when the post-create goodsouts lookup returns empty instead of an IndexError. Verifying a write fix needs a working sandbox.

`test_get_shipping_methods_perm_validator` (then named `test_get_shipping_methods_auth_code`) failed in [Daily CI run 515](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/30281811342>) with `Failed: Timeout (>240.0s) from pytest-timeout`, and reproduces locally in the full auth run (1 failed / 6 passed / 3 skipped, 452s).

`get_shipping_methods` fetches the carrier list, then issues one `carriers/{id}/carrier_services` request per carrier, serially. Measured against the test connection:

```
carriers=84 fetch=1.0s
  carrier 929: 1.2s
  carrier 963: 1.0s
  carrier 1068: 0.9s
  carrier 1069: 0.9s
  carrier 1499: 1.0s
avg per carrier=1.0s -> projected total=87s
```

So the walk costs somewhere north of 87 seconds of pure round-trip time before any latency variance. That is comfortably inside 240s on a good run (the non-auth `test_get_shipping_methods` passed in the same session) and over it on a bad one, which is why this flips between runs rather than failing consistently. Under the daily suite's `-n 32` parallelism the per-request latency is worse than measured here.

Not a defect in the auth-code path: `fc_request` is identical with and without an auth code, and `get_shipping_methods` never touches stored resources. The unrelated auth-code bug in `get_orders` was fixed in [trackstarhq/pokedex#5196](https://linear.app/trackstar-hq/review/fix-tests-2026-07-27-excelsior-product-path-and-fulfilmentcrowd-auth-00b69127056c); this one is untouched by that change.

Wants a decision on how to make the walk cheaper, since no bulk carrier-services endpoint is in use today. Deliberately not attempted in the fix-tests sweep: it is a performance change to a shipping path, not a test fix, and it wants its own verification.

input.description:
`test_create_return` fails against a healthy sandbox host with the vendor rejecting the return:

```
PokedexException: {"error":{"message":"Order not found.","specifics":{"data":{
  "http_status":400,"code":"V5-ORDER-INVALID-ORDER","message":"Order not found."}}}}
```

Cause looks like the test fixture, not the integration. `TestIFulfilment.full_return` sets `reference_id` to a fresh `uuid.uuid4().hex`, and `create_return` posts that straight through as the `reference` on `POST /v1/orders/returns`. A random reference matches no order, so the vendor is right to reject it. A return needs the reference of an order that actually exists, presumably the one `test_create_order` just created (which is available via `context`, and note `create_order` reads the reference back off the response as `full_order_ref`, so the vendor may not echo the reference it was given).

This has been failing for a while but was masked. While the sandbox host was hanging it surfaced as `Failed: Timeout (>60.0s) from pytest-timeout`, so it read as part of the outage. With the host healthy the whole suite now runs in 56s and this is the only remaining failure: 1 failed, 21 passed, 26 skipped.

`test_get_inventory_perm_validator`, `test_get_inbound_shipments_perm_validator` and `test_get_orders_perm_validator` (named `..._auth_code` before #5891) all hit the 240 second test timeout on the same SFTP read, while the connection-based versions of all three pass. The test's no-connection fixture makes the "files we already handled" list come back empty, so the read pulls down the whole RJW folder (680 files) instead of the 21 new ones.

Someone needs to pick between giving that fixture a connection id, which is shared test machinery every integration uses, and capping what one crawl reads, which changes real crawls. Evidence is in [trackstarhq/pokedex#6004](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/pull/6004>).

`get_all_items` pages Walmart's whole item catalog in one uninterrupted loop, Walmart 429s partway through, and the wait it asks for pushes the test past its 240 second budget. Failed in [runs 539 and 540](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/33194053322>) and reproduces locally with `ThrottleException: Walmart rate limit exceeded`.

It cannot simply pause and resume: the code walks the catalog in one go precisely because the cursor expires after two minutes, which is shorter than the throttle wait. Someone needs to decide how get_products should page a large catalog under the rate limit.

`api-summary.md` explains why: `get_integration_secret` rebuilds the whole secret on every token re-mint, so any code that did not know the key silently dropped it. That code is now on `main`, so the key should survive from here. The TEST value is `166`.

Someone with the OrderWise credentials needs to re-install the dev connection so the secret carries `goods_in_export_id`. It cannot be done from the agent container, which does not hold the vendor credentials.

input.description:
`test_get_invoice_line_items_perm_validator` (then named `..._auth_code`) failed for both fedex and ups in [Daily CI run 539](<https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/actions/runs/33095445523>) and reproduces locally.

```text
AssertionError: no browser session open; use session()
transports/browser/crawl.py:184
```

The test is new: it came in with 432e689 "add cart permission tests (#5774)", merged after run 538. It surfaced a gap that has been there all along rather than causing one.

`CarrierIntegration.get_invoice_line_items` runs the crawl through `self.browser_crawl.run_page(...)`, which asserts a session is already open. The only thing that opens one is the crawler's `crawl_scope()`. Permission validation calls the get function directly, with no crawl around it, so it has never had a session. In production the permission validator catches the error and records `failed_to_test: True`, so nobody sees it: we simply never learn whether a fedex or ups connection can read invoices. Only these two carriers are affected because only they raise permissions exceptions, which is what makes the validator run at all.

Not fixed in the sweep because the fix belongs in `integrations/carrier/CarrierIntegration.py`, a shared base that all six carrier integrations use, and the fix-tests scope is one integration's own directory. Duplicating a workaround into fedex and ups separately would be worse.

The shape that would work: in `get_invoice_line_items`, when no session is open, use `browser_crawl.run(...)` (which opens and tears one down) instead of `run_page(...)`. Someone should decide between that and having the carrier test skip browser-backed integrations, since the first also changes what permission validation costs at install time.

```

Test: test/integrations/carrier/ups_test.py::TestUps::test_get_invoice_line_items_perm_validator
```

50	    not_passed = set()

60	        )

# Code style (pokedex Python)

The always-on subset, consolidated from CLAUDE.md and `integration-patterns.md` "Code style". Full reviewer checklist (incl. advisory / new-build-only items like `while True`, guard clauses, inline dict values): `.claude/references/integration-patterns.md` "Code style".

- **No docstrings, with two exceptions.** Pokedex code is self-documenting. Both exceptions are where the docstring is published text, not a comment: `api.py` endpoint handlers, whose docstring is the endpoint's OpenAPI summary and description (the rollout pushes that spec to Mintlify and Svix, so it is the public API docs, and every public endpoint carries one); Alembic migration modules under `migrations/versions/`, which keep the generated header (title, `Revision ID`, `Revises`, `Create Date`) plus a line of rationale when the schema change is not obvious from the operations. Nothing under `integrations/`, `utils/`, `resources/`, or `actions/` has one.
- **Default to no comment; when in doubt, delete.** A comment exists only when the change is not obvious from the code alone. If the code, a variable name, or the error message beside it already says it, the comment is noise — delete it rather than polish it. That covers narration ("sum the quantities per sku"), section labels, and anything restating an assert or a raise.
- **Comments: lowercase, ≤2 lines, why not what.** Vendor quirks, surprising invariants, non-obvious couplings. Vendor field names keep their original casing inside a lowercase comment (`DeliveryNotes` stays `DeliveryNotes`) — lowercasing them breaks the reference. The ceiling yields only when a genuinely non-obvious vendor data model or a disambiguating example needs the room and nothing shorter carries it. The same ceiling applies to raised error messages — a `PokedexException` says what went wrong and what to do in a line or two, not a paragraph.
- **ELI5, no jargon.** Write it the way you'd say it out loud to an engineer new to the codebase: plain words any SWE understands cold, in one read. No noun-stacks ("multi-lot pick collision"), no arrow chains (`x → y → z`), no model-speak ("ensure correctness", "for clarity", "leverage"), no clever compression that needs decoding ("must not look like it did"). "with no batch number, picks from different batches get combined here, so we can't keep a single expiry date" beats "blank-batch multi-lot picks collapse under the package uniqueness key, dropping the expiry anchor".
- **Comments are self-contained.** Never reference `api-summary.md`, any `.claude/...` file, doctrine vocabulary ("tier-3", "shallow-fix", "per integration-patterns"), or the authoring agent. A reader at HEAD with only this file open must understand it.
- **Comments never name** customer orgs, the source integration a pattern was copied from, or observation dates — those leak or rot. The ban is on customers: naming the integration's own vendor inside its own files is normal. Rich rationale (customer, pattern source, load-bearing dates) lives in `api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions". Exception: vendor/3PL support-contact lines inside `support()` — naming contacts is that method's job.
- **Raise, don't `assert`.** Runtime error paths raise `PokedexException` (or the typed `create_*` exception helpers), never `assert` — asserts strip under `python -O` and carry no status or origin. `assert` belongs in tests only.
- **A package `__init__.py` that re-exports lists those names in `__all__`.** Re-exports are the point of the file, but every one of them reads as an unused import to the linter, so the list is what keeps it quiet and doubles as the package's public surface. Add a name in both places or the linter flags it again.
- **No `@property` on anything a subclass overrides.** A value an integration can change is a plain method, so every call site shows it's dispatched rather than read off the instance. `@property` is still fine for something defined once and never overridden (`staging_key`, `bucket`). Name a boolean method for how it reads at the call site — `uses_browserbase()`, not `use_browserbase()`.
- **No `ABC` / `@abstractmethod`.** A base class declares a method subclasses must supply by raising `NotImplementedError` in the body, with a short message saying what the subclass owes. That's the one pattern used everywhere else, and on integrations it's load-bearing: `BaseIntegration.is_implemented` reads a method's source looking for that raise to decide which functions an integration supports, so an abstract stub would be read as implemented and get scheduled.
- **UPPER_CASE names are module-level only.** A constant-style value scoped inside a function is a lowercase local like any other; capitals are reserved for module-level constants (status maps, page sizes, vendor tunables).
- **No leading-underscore "private" names** on methods, attributes, or locals. Underscore privacy isn't enforced here and signals nothing. If a class helper needs `self` it's a method; if not, hoist it module-level; if used once, inline it. (Dunders like `__init__` are exempt.)
- **Error-driven: avoid `.get()` — on vendor-response reads.** Loud failures (a `KeyError` during `yarn crawl`) are how we learn real API behavior. `.get(field, default)` on a vendor response is allowed only after observing the field is genuinely sometimes-absent. Nullable is not optional: a key the vendor always sends but sometimes nulls is read with a direct index (plus an `or` fallback when a default is needed) — `.get()` there misstates the contract by implying the key can be missing. The rule does not cover reads where absence is the normal, documented case — optional fields of a validated write payload in `create_*`/`update_*` methods, marshmallow `query_data` in API handlers (absent optional params are omitted from the dict), and our own state attributes that most rows don't carry — there `.get()` is the convention and is self-documenting. Comment a `.get()` only when the absence is surprising (the contract says the field should be there and observation proved otherwise: `# vendor returns null for unfulfilled orders`); a `.get()` on a documented-optional field needs no comment.
- **No list/dict comprehensions in integration code.** Use multi-line `for` loops with named intermediates — comprehensions are opaque under `pdb`.
- **No `logger.info` / `print` in integration code** (carrier is the documented exception — its async/queued flows justify checkpoint logging). Every other type stays quiet: Datadog spans + connection-error rows are the observability surface; `logger.warning`/`error` only for genuinely surprising, actionable states.
- **Platform constants live in `config.py`.** Feature modules `import config`; don't scatter `os.environ.get`. Integration-level constants (status maps, page sizes, vendor base URLs, per-vendor tunables) stay in the integration's own module — they're hard to unify across vendors and don't belong in the shared config.
- **Favor simplicity over cleverness — and the smallest fix that addresses the root cause.** A fix that adds new mechanisms (a helper, a wrapper, a retry layer, config) where editing an existing line suffices is overengineered and gets rejected in review. Before inventing a new shape, check how neighboring integrations already solve the same problem and match it. The same bar applies to edge cases: a narrow race or double-failure edge that self-corrects on the next cycle (or whose outcome is still correct for the user) is documented — or made observable with a log line — not engineered around with new state machines or guards.

- **Reuse the codebase's words; never coin a verb.** A name is found, not composed: before naming a function, helper, constant, status value, or table, grep for how neighbors name the same operation on the same kind of thing (`rg -n 'def \w+_<noun>\b'`, `rg -n 'def \w+_row\b'`) and pick from the verbs that come back; the search is by object, never by a list of verbs, because a list is itself a vocabulary that drifts. Dynamo row helpers are `create_ / get_ / update_ / store_ / delete_<thing>_row`. Under `integrations/`, data-function and action names come from the resource and action contracts, so there is nothing to choose. A status string is the word the API's error text uses for that state (`unconfirmed` when the 409 says "could not be confirmed"), so the row, the log line, and the error read the same. A word from one recent feature is not established vocabulary; count its uses across the repo before adopting it. Payments, ops, and distributed-systems jargon (`settle`, `claim`, `release`, `landed`, `in flight`, `ambiguous`, `reconcile`) is a coined verb here unless the grep shows it already carries that meaning in this codebase. Say what the code does in words the code already uses: `mark_<row>_succeeded`, `store_write_ids_for_replay`, `write_may_have_reached_vendor`.
- **Comments and error messages use the code's own names.** A comment names the function, status, and field exactly as the code spells them and describes the mechanism in the same verbs. A comment that introduces a second vocabulary for the thing beside it is rewritten in the code's words or deleted.

## Running code & tests
- **Tests: only `yarn test` with filters.** Never `python -m pytest` or raw `pytest`. Scopes/markers: `.claude/skills/run-scripts/guides/test.md`.
- **Ad-hoc Python: `uv run python3`.** Never raw `python3`/`python` — dependencies resolve through `uv`.

- **UPPER_CASE names are module-level only.** A constant-style value scoped inside a function is a lowercase local like any other; capitals are reserved for module-level constants (status maps, page sizes, vendor tunables).
- **No leading-underscore "private" names** on methods, attributes, or locals. Underscore privacy isn't enforced here and signals nothing. If a class helper needs `self` it's a method; if not, hoist it module-level; if used once, inline it. (Dunders like `__init__` are exempt.)
- **Error-driven: avoid `.get()` — on vendor-response reads.** Loud failures (a `KeyError` during `yarn crawl`) are how we learn real API behavior. `.get(field, default)` on a vendor response is allowed only after observing the field is genuinely sometimes-absent. Nullable is not optional: a key the vendor always sends but sometimes nulls is read with a direct index (plus an `or` fallback when a default is needed) — `.get()` there misstates the contract by implying the key can be missing. The rule does not cover reads where absence is the normal, documented case — optional fields of a validated write payload in `create_*`/`update_*` methods, marshmallow `query_data` in API handlers (absent optional params are omitted from the dict), and our own state attributes that most rows don't carry — there `.get()` is the convention and is self-documenting. Comment a `.get()` only when the absence is surprising (the contract says the field should be there and observation proved otherwise: `# vendor returns null for unfulfilled orders`); a `.get()` on a documented-optional field needs no comment.
- **No list/dict comprehensions in integration code.** Use multi-line `for` loops with named intermediates — comprehensions are opaque under `pdb`.
- **No `logger.info` / `print` in integration code** (carrier is the documented exception — its async/queued flows justify checkpoint logging). Every other type stays quiet: Datadog spans + connection-error rows are the observability surface; `logger.warning`/`error` only for genuinely surprising, actionable states.
- **Platform constants live in `config.py`.** Feature modules `import config`; don't scatter `os.environ.get`. Integration-level constants (status maps, page sizes, vendor base URLs, per-vendor tunables) stay in the integration's own module — they're hard to unify across vendors and don't belong in the shared config.
- **Favor simplicity over cleverness — and the smallest fix that addresses the root cause.** A fix that adds new mechanisms (a helper, a wrapper, a retry layer, config) where editing an existing line suffices is overengineered and gets rejected in review. Before inventing a new shape, check how neighboring integrations already solve the same problem and match it. The same bar applies to edge cases: a narrow race or double-failure edge that self-corrects on the next cycle (or whose outcome is still correct for the user) is documented — or made observable with a log line — not engineered around with new state machines or guards.

- **Reuse the codebase's words; never coin a verb.** A name is found, not composed: before naming a function, helper, constant, status value, or table, grep for how neighbors name the same operation on the same kind of thing (`rg -n 'def \w+_<noun>\b'`, `rg -n 'def \w+_row\b'`) and pick from the verbs that come back; the search is by object, never by a list of verbs, because a list is itself a vocabulary that drifts. Dynamo row helpers are `create_ / get_ / update_ / store_ / delete_<thing>_row`. Under `integrations/`, data-function and action names come from the resource and action contracts, so there is nothing to choose. A status string is the word the API's error text uses for that state (`unconfirmed` when the 409 says "could not be confirmed"), so the row, the log line, and the error read the same. A word from one recent feature is not established vocabulary; count its uses across the repo before adopting it. Payments, ops, and distributed-systems jargon (`settle`, `claim`, `release`, `landed`, `in flight`, `ambiguous`, `reconcile`) is a coined verb here unless the grep shows it already carries that meaning in this codebase. Say what the code does in words the code already uses: `mark_<row>_succeeded`, `store_write_ids_for_replay`, `write_may_have_reached_vendor`.
- **Comments and error messages use the code's own names.** A comment names the function, status, and field exactly as the code spells them and describes the mechanism in the same verbs. A comment that introduces a second vocabulary for the thing beside it is rewritten in the code's words or deleted.

content.text:
Both done.

**Backfill.** All 17 open `fix-tests` cards that the reconciler could never close are fixed in Linear: 12 got their first `Test:` line (TRA-2777, 2715, 2713, 2712, 2711, 2683, 2650, 2567, 2419, 2383, 2369, 2309), 2 had `yarn test -k thing` swapped for real node ids (TRA-2755, 2754), and 2 carried node ids that #5891 renamed from `*_auth_code` to `*_perm_validator` (TRA-2899, 2774) — a stale name is invisible to the reconciler in exactly the same way a missing line is. Every id was checked against the current test files before writing.

Five were deliberately left without lines, because a green suite wouldn't mean they're fixed: TRA-2714 (clarus ledger reversals, no test tracks it), TRA-2682 (rush-order, the real ask is the 5xx-to-ThrottleException mapping, not the outage), TRA-2583 (shippingbo credential-leak check, fails at random ~0.6% of runs), and TRA-2734/TRA-2716, the "Daily CI run N" summary cards the 1.7 contract outlawed.

**Enforcement** — [#6178](https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/pull/6178), draft:
- `create-linear-issue` spec mode now refuses a `fix-tests` card with no `Test:` line, the same way it already refuses a missing label. That's the one chokepoint every card goes through.
- `fix-tests` says to copy the node id out of the run you just did, with the command that prints it (`yarn test -k <name> --collect-only -q -q`), rather than from the CI report's wording or an older card.
- `scripts/reconcile_test_cards.py` logs every open card it can never close and why, so the drift shows up in the daily run instead of silently. 22 tests pass.

One thing to know: the working tree had uncommitted edits to `integrations/wms/{jaygroup,shipnetwork,warehouseos}` and `warehouseos_test.py` before I started. I left them alone and kept them out of the commit, but they're still sitting on the `fix-tests-card-test-lines` branch.

Usage:  `yarn routine [<routine-name>] [--text TEXT | --text-file PATH] [--id ID --token TOKEN] [-h|--help]`
Fire a Claude Code routine through its /fire endpoint. Name a known routine to
resolve its {"id", "token"} from Secrets Manager, or pass an ad-hoc routine's
id + token (via --id/--token or routine.json) with no name. POSTs the text payload
(passed to the routine unparsed, alongside its saved prompt).
Arguments:
    routine-name        A known routine to fire (one of: %s). Omit to use ad-hoc id + token.
Options:
    --text              Text passed to the routine (overrides routine.json)
    --text-file         Read the text payload from a file (overrides routine.json)
    --id                Ad-hoc routine id (overrides routine.json; not with a routine name)
    --token             Ad-hoc routine /fire token (overrides routine.json; not with a routine name)
    -h, --help          Show this help text
routine.json (optional; CLI args override these):
    {
        "text": "the text to pass to the routine",
        "id": "trig_...",            # ad-hoc only: a custom routine's id
        "token": "sk-ant-oat01-..."  # ad-hoc only: its /fire token
    }
""" % ", ".join(sorted(ROUTINE_SECRETS))


def load_params():
    if os.path.exists("routine.json"):
        with open("routine.json") as f:
            return json.load(f)
    return {}


def resolve_text(cli_text, cli_text_file, params):
    if cli_text_file:
        with open(cli_text_file) as f:
            return f.read()
    if cli_text is not None:
        return cli_text
    return params.get("text")


def flag_value(args, i, flag):
    # a following flag means the value is missing — fail rather than consume it
    if i + 1 >= len(args) or args[i + 1].startswith("-"):
        print_red(f"Error: {flag} requires a value")
    return args[i + 1]


def main():
    routine_name = None
    cli_text = None

Assigned 24 of the 36 open PRs; the rest were already assigned or have nobody to assign to.

**Authors (20).** Every human-authored PR with an empty assignee now has its author: joe-trackstar (6187, 6122, 5851, 5811, 5577, 4210), keerthi-trackstar (6183, 6173, 6165, 6156, 6153, 6152, 5908, 4379), hnandiwada (6178, 6166, 5888), sam-trackstar (6182, 6038), DanielLanger (5657). PRs 6042, 5772 and 3841 already had assignees, so I left them.

**trackstardev (4 resolved via Linear).** 6118 → sam-trackstar (TRA-2956), 5957 → sam-trackstar (TRA-2869), 5897 → DrewZucker (TRA-2841), 5812 → DrewZucker (TRA-2770).

**trackstardev (9 left unassigned), because Linear has no human on them either:**

| PR | Linear | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| 6188 | TRA-2890 Blocked | issue unassigned |
| 6185 | TRA-2831 Blocked | assigned to dev@trackstarhq.com, the bot itself |
| 6105 | TRA-2936 Blocked | issue unassigned |
| 6064 | TRA-2888 Blocked | issue unassigned |
| 5992 | TRA-2612 Ready | issue unassigned |
| 6181, 6150, 6137, 5844 | none | no Linear issue attached to the PR at all |

Tell me who owns those and I'll set them.

**On a daily routine: I'd not use one.** The rule is mechanical for human PRs, so it belongs at PR-open time, not in a nightly sweep: a ~10-line workflow on `pull_request: opened` that assigns `github.event.pull_request.user.login` unless the author is trackstardev. That leaves zero strays instead of up to a day of them, and costs no agent run.

The bot half doesn't fit a sweep either. Five of the nine I couldn't place have a Linear issue that is itself unassigned, so a nightly job would re-derive "nobody" every night and never converge. The better place is the skills that open those PRs — `plan-integration`, `fix-tests`, `stale-schedule-investigate` already know which Linear issue fired them, so they can set the assignee at creation when the issue has one. The genuine gap is upstream: bot-build issues get worked without anyone being assigned in Linear.

Want me to add the open-time workflow, and the assignee step to the PR-opening skills?

Two of the three are valid; the P2 on shipnetwork is wrong.

**P1, `create-linear-issue/SKILL.md:76` — valid, and it's my wording.** I wrote the form as `path/to/file_test.py::TestClass::test_name`, which excludes module-level ids. That's not hypothetical: yesterday I backfilled TRA-2419 with three of them (`test/api/api_test.py::test_filters`, `::test_indexes`, `::test_sandbox_simulate_fulfill`), and the reconciler handles them on purpose — `node_id` falls back to `f"{path}::{name}"` when the classname doesn't match the module (`scripts/reconcile_test_cards.py:43`), and there's a test pinning parametrized ids with spaces. So the gate as written would reject cards the closer can actually close. One-line reword: name the exact id pytest prints, with both shapes as examples.

**P2, `jaygroup/integration.py:493` — valid but trivial.** `wh_map = {wh.lower(): wh for wh in WAREHOUSES}` is a new dict comprehension in integration code, which `code-style.md` bans. The suggested loop is behavior-identical. Worth noting the file already has comprehensions a few lines down (`shipment_line_items`), untouched, so this is a rule that only binds the new line. Your call whether it's worth the churn; the map itself is arguably unnecessary, since the loop below could iterate `WAREHOUSES` directly and compare `wh.lower()`.

**P2, `shipnetwork/integration.py:34` — wrong.** It claims `TestShipnetwork` inherits `allow_writes() == True`. It doesn't: the commit Greptile reviewed (027352c81, the branch HEAD) is the one that adds

```python
def allow_writes(self):
    return False
```

to `test/integrations/wms/shipnetwork_test.py:10`. Greptile read the integration file's new `test_account()` string, flagged the risk from that alone, and missed the test file in the same diff. Reply and dismiss.

One thing the review didn't catch: the branch now carries jaygroup, shipnetwork and warehouseos edits on top of my skill/reconciler commit, but the PR body still says `test override: `yarn test nonints``, so CI will not run any of those three integrations' tests. Either split the integration work into its own PR or widen the override to `yarn test nonints -k jaygroup -k shipnetwork -k warehouseos`.

Want me to fix the P1 wording and reply to the shipnetwork comment?
